prompt_text: I need a personal injury lawyer in Charlotte after a car accident. Which specific law firms should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Charlotte for a car accident case?
answer_verbatim:
I can do that — I’ll give you a short, targeted list of specific Charlotte personal-injury firms to call plus why each is a good fit. First, two quick questions so I recommend the best firms for your situation:

1. What ZIP code or neighborhood in/near Charlotte are you in? (I’ll prioritize firms with offices close to you.)  
2. How serious are your injuries (minor, moderate, severe/long-term), and do you expect to need surgery or long-term care?  

If you want an immediate general answer without those details, I can still give a curated list of well-regarded Charlotte personal injury firms and what to ask when you call — say which you prefer.

Meanwhile, here are practical next steps and what to ask every lawyer when you call (so you can compare quickly):

What to do now (immediately)
- Seek medical care and follow treatment; medical records are critical.  
- Get a copy of the police report and preserve photos/video of the crash scene, damage, injuries, and any skid marks.  
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the insurer or accept the first settlement offer. Notify your insurer of the crash but keep statements factual.  
- Note the other driver’s insurer and policy limits if you can.

What to ask each lawyer (quick checklist)
- Do you handle car-accident/personal-injury cases in Charlotte? (Yes/No)  
- Who will handle my case (attorney name) and will it go to a paralegal?  
- Do you take cases on contingency (no fee unless you recover)? What percent?  
- Do you have trial experience in Mecklenburg County? (If needed, is the firm willing to take it to trial?)  
- Typical settlement/award range for cases like mine (ballpark).  
- How long do you expect the case to take?  
- Will you advance upfront costs (medical record fees, expert fees) or do I pay them?  
- How often will I get updates and who is my point of contact?  
- Any conflicts or reasons you can’t take my case?  
- Do you represent people against insurance companies (not the other driver)?  

Red flags when you call
- The attorney/firm won’t give a clear answer about contingency fees or who actually handles the case.  
- No trial experience or unwillingness to try cases if necessary.  
- Pressure to sign immediately, or promises of a specific dollar outcome.  
- Poor communication at intake (long delays, no follow-up).

If you want me to produce a concrete list now, say “Yes — give me firms” and confirm your ZIP or neighborhood and severity of injuries. I’ll then provide 6–10 specific Charlotte firms to call and one-sentence reasons for each (experience, trial record, free consults, local reputation).
